title: exec-staff-meeting-prep-notes-2026-03-22
content:
Exec staff weekly sync - prep notes (2026-03-22)

Time: 09:00-10:00 PT
Attendees (expected): Avery Chen (chair), Samir Patel, Lina Alvarez, Priya Singh, Marcus Lee, Elena Kovacs, hiring update from People Ops (TBD)
\Goals for the meeting:
- Quick alignment on SLOs / any regressions since last week
- Decide on Dedicated autoscaling policy tweak to reduce P95 latency spikes during bursts
- Pilot status: private deployment (Acme Corp) and next steps for on-prem package
- Surface GTM ask for increased Dedicated capacity for two mid-size customers
- Review outstanding action items and owners
\1) Metrics & platform health (Samir)
- Current brief: p50 gen latency ~ 68ms, p95 ~ 210-240ms (higher during 17:00-19:00 PT window)
- Error rate: 0.8% (mainly transient GPUOOMs on one Dedicated pool last Tues)
- Cost: average token cost per 1k ~ $0.055 (hosted) - Optimize recommendations in Optimize queue
- Notes to call out: increased tail latency correlates with larger sequence length requests from a small set of customers (see: ENG-1024)
\Talking points:
- Do we accept a small increase in p50 (target up to +10%) in exchange for a 25% drop in cost via more aggressive batching? (Product + SRE input needed)
- Are the GPUOOMs mitigated by current autoscaler changes? We need the SRE postmortem draft before the meeting.
\2) Dedicated capacity / renewals (Lina)
- Renewal negotiation with two customers (RetailCo, FinSuite) - both asking for committed QPS and stricter latency SLA
- Proposal: offer reserved pools with canary capacity + optional burst credits (pricing appendix in Confluence)
- Risk: if we overcommit without better autoscale controls, we expose ourselves to weekly tail incidents
\Decision needed: Approve Lina to present a limited-risk term (60% guaranteed, 40% burst on demand) to both customers.
\3) Private deployment pilot (Priya)
- Acme pilot: initial on-prem install completed 3/15, running validation suite; feature parity gap: kms integration and audit logs retention config
- Blocker: customer wants HSM key wrapping (timeline unknown) - engineering estimate: 3-4 sprints to support full HSM integration
\Ask for meeting: Approve a commercial interim (managed KMS proxy) while engineering builds HSM; legal to review contract clause (privacy / audit).
\4) Outage / incident review (Marcus/Elena)
- Mini-incident last Tue: one Dedicated pool hit OOM on longer context requests; fallback to hosted succeeded but with 2-3s added latency for affected customers
- Action: improved request-size throttling + KV cache tuning deployed; need to monitor for 72 hours
\5) GTM / Sales updates (Elena)
- Sales pipeline: 3 mid-size deals pushing for dedicated capacity by EoQ; revenue ops needs capacity confirmation by 03/29 to hit commitments
- Ask: can we provision extra 2 reserved pools in us-west region by 03/26? Cost estimate required (Lina + infra)
\6) People / hiring quick check (Avery)
- Org ask: one senior infra SRE req approved; recruiting to prioritize (Marcus to own)
\Parking lot / topics for later
- Long-term autoscaling strategy (batch-aware + customer-priority routing) - schedule separate deep dive
- Quantization and quality regressions: how we measure before recommending more aggressive quant profiles
\Outstanding action items (for follow-up in meeting):
- Samir: bring 7-day latency/error dashboard and quick root-cause summary for the P95 regression (due 2026-03-24)
- Lina: draft renewal term with limited-risk burst option + cost appendix (due 2026-03-25)
- Priya: propose managed-KMS interim and updated contract language for legal review (linked: Confluence 123456789) (due 2026-03-24)
- Marcus: accelerate SRE postmortem + mitigation timeline for GPUOOMs, include runbook changes (due 2026-03-24)
- Elena: confirm sales asks and list deals requiring capacity by 03/29; provide estimated committed QPS per deal (due 2026-03-23)
- People Ops (Hannah): send candidate shortlist and hiring timeline for senior infra SRE (due 2026-03-26)
\Open questions to raise in the meeting:
- Policy trade-off: aggressive batching vs strict latency SLOs - what is customer tolerance? (ask Sales to surface top 5 customers impacted)
- Can we use Dedicated burst credits as a contractual lever to smooth demand while not overcommitting physical capacity?
\Prep / attachments to bring:
- Samir: link to live dashboard (Confluence + Grafana) and quick slides (2 slides) on latency trends
- Lina: pricing appendix and sample contract language (Confluence: SALES-210)
- Priya: pilot status doc and list of missing features for private (Confluence: PRIVATE-332)
\Notes to self / things to call out during meeting:
- Keep discussion outcome-oriented: either quick approval for Lina's limited-risk renewal term or assign a negotiation pilot owner.
- If engineering cannot promise HSM timelines, be prepared to offer a paid-managed-KMS interim for Acme (short-term revenue win).
- Avoid deep technical deep dives in exec sync; take complex items offline to SRE/product sessions.
\Post-meeting follow-ups (template to send within 24h):
- Short email summary with decisions + updated action item tracker (Avery to send)
- Update Confluence page with final renewal terms and pilot status (Lina / Priya)
\---
Rough draft of the 2-slide summary for the meeting (for Samir):
Slide 1: Platform health snapshot (p50/p95, error rate trend, top 3 customers by request size)
Slide 2: Decision items (autoscaling tweak approve? Dedicated burst approach?) + immediate mitigations deployed
\Misc quick notes:
- Linked tickets: ENG-1024 (latency regression investigation), PRIVATE-332 (Acme pilot), SALES-210 (renewals), SRE-501 (OOM postmortem)
- Slack threads: #ops-alerts (OOM thread), #sales-enterprise (RetailCo negotiation)
\End of prep notes.
\Drafted by: Avery Chen
Status: DRAFT - will update after sync
